name: Ninhle AI Sales Assistant – AI Chatbot for WooCommerce
author: Ninh Le

sections.description:
Turn shopper questions into orders. Ninhle AI Sales Assistant is an AI chatbot for WooCommerce: a shopping assistant for your customers and a sales assistant for you. It answers in seconds from the prices, stock and product details already in your store, looks up orders, brings in your team when needed, and shows you which orders followed a chat.

Shoppers ask the same things all day: Is it in stock? Does it come in M? How long is shipping? Where is my order? When nobody answers, many of them leave. Unlike a generic ecommerce chatbot that only knows what it was trained on, this WooCommerce chatbot answers from live lookups against your store, and says so when it does not know.

Get started in three steps

  1. Connect an AI provider. Paste your own API key from OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude) or Google (Gemini). You pay the provider directly. Or start in local-only mode with no key at all.
  2. Sync your catalog. One click, or wp ninhle-ai-sales-assistant sync-products, and the assistant knows your products, prices and stock.
  3. Go live. The chat appears on your store with your name, logo, colour and suggested questions.

An AI chatbot that answers from your real catalog

Product facts come from your WooCommerce store: prices, stock, product details, store policies and your own pages. If the catalog has not been synced, the assistant says so and offers a person instead of guessing. It never invents prices or stock.

A shopping assistant that sells, not just chats

An editable sales playbook sets the tone, the qualifying questions, how to handle objections and how to close. The assistant recommends products from your catalog and links shoppers straight to them, so a question turns into a product page, a cart and a checkout.

Order tracking in the chat

Customers ask “Where is my order?” and get the status right in the chat once they give the order number with the email or phone number used for it. Nobody on your team has to look it up.

A person is one tap away

“Talk to a person” is always visible, and the assistant hands off complaints, explicit requests and answers it is not sure about. Your team replies from the Inbox in WP Admin, and a webhook you choose can be notified.

See the orders the chatbot helped close

The AI Value & Performance tab shows what the AI cost, how many orders followed a chat and how conversations ended, each with its sample size, from the day you install. Leads left in the chat stay in your own database and export to CSV.

Your key, your data, no per-conversation fee

Use your own OpenAI, Anthropic Claude or Google Gemini API key and pay the provider directly. Requests go from your server to that provider; there is no middleman server and no per-chat fee from us. Simple greetings and store policy, cart and order-status questions are answered from store data without an AI call whenever the store has the answer, which keeps the cost down.

Everything in the free WooCommerce chatbot

  • Bring your own key: Anthropic Claude, OpenAI or Google Gemini. You control the account and the spend.
  • Store tools: product search and details, order status (only after the customer proves they own the order), digital downloads, store policies and site content.
  • Sales playbook and rules: persona, qualifying questions, objection handling and closing, plus keyword rules for instant answers.
  • Lead capture: a contact form in the chat, with leads stored in your database and exportable to CSV.
  • Human handoff: visitors always see whether they are talking to the AI assistant, waiting for your team or talking to a team member. A webhook URL you choose can be notified.
  • AI Value & Performance: AI cost recorded per request from your provider’s usage data and a dated price table; orders that followed a chat; conversations resolved (confirmed by the customer), handed off or unresolved.
  • Conversation inbox: read every conversation, take over from the bot and hand the chat back when you are done.
  • Formatted answers: bold text, lists, tables, links and product images display cleanly in the chat.
  • Voice input (optional, off by default): visitors can speak their message; the browser turns it into text they check before sending.
  • Your brand: widget name, logo, colour, font and suggested question chips, with a live preview.
  • Local-only mode: answer product, cart and order questions from store data without calling any AI provider.
  • Light on your pages: the chat window loads only when a visitor opens it.
  • Privacy built in: WordPress personal-data export and erasure, attachment retention, rate limiting.
  • Translation-ready: every string can be translated on translate.wordpress.org.
  • WooCommerce compatible: supports High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) and the Cart and Checkout blocks.

Optional paid plans

Ninhle AI Sales Assistant is free to install and use. Optional paid plans add extra code to the
plugin; nothing in the free version is locked or time-limited.

Starter — product variations with per-variation add-to-cart links, Telegram
notifications for new leads and handoffs, a sales dashboard, cached answers
for repeated questions, and the revenue of orders that followed a chat, per currency,
on the AI Value & Performance tab.

Pro — everything in Starter, plus coupon validation, automatic failover to a
second AI provider, daily and monthly AI budget caps, rule-based lead scoring with
advanced analytics, price-output verification, and signed HMAC-SHA256 webhooks
for n8n, Make, Zapier and CRMs.

AI usage is never included: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google bill you directly for
your own API key, on every plan including Free.

External services

The plugin connects to the services below. Except for the AI provider you configure,
each one is used only when you turn the related setting on.

AI provider (the one you configure) — receives the visitor’s chat messages, recent
conversation history, your sales playbook and business information, and product data from
your own store, each time a visitor sends a message. Nothing is sent in local-only mode.

  • Anthropic (Claude) — https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy — https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms
  • OpenAI — https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy — https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use
  • Google (Gemini) — https://policies.google.com/privacy — https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms

Link reading (optional, off by default) — when you enable “Let the bot read links
customers send”, a URL a visitor pastes into the chat is sent to r.jina.ai to fetch its
text (https://jina.ai/legal/). YouTube links are read from youtube.com instead, to get the
video title and public transcript (https://policies.google.com/privacy,
https://www.youtube.com/t/terms). Leave this off if visitors might paste private links.

Google Fonts (optional) — only if you pick a Google font for the widget in the
settings. Visitors’ browsers then load that font from fonts.googleapis.com
(https://policies.google.com/privacy). The default font loads nothing from Google.

Voice input (optional, off by default) — only if you turn on “Let visitors speak their
message”. The microphone button uses the speech recognition built into the visitor’s own browser
(Web Speech API). Depending on the browser, the audio may be sent to the browser maker’s speech
recognition service, for example Google for Chrome (https://policies.google.com/privacy), Apple
for Safari (https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/) or Microsoft for Edge
(https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement). The plugin never receives, records or stores
audio; it only receives the text the visitor chooses to send.

Handoff webhook (optional) — only if you enter a webhook URL. On a handoff the plugin
sends the conversation ID, contact ID and handoff level to that URL, which you control.

Telegram (paid plans only, optional) — the free version contains no Telegram code. In
the Starter and Pro plans, if you enter a Telegram bot token and chat ID, new leads (name,
email, phone) and handoff requests (priority, issue, summary, conversation number) are sent
to api.telegram.org (https://telegram.org/privacy, https://telegram.org/tos).

Automation webhooks (Pro plan only, optional) — the free version contains no code for
this. In Pro, if you enter a webhook URL, lead and handoff events are posted to that URL,
which you control, signed with your secret.

Freemius (licensing, upgrades and affiliate program) — the plugin bundles the Freemius
SDK. Nothing is sent to Freemius from your storefront. The plugin contacts Freemius only
when an administrator does one of the following:

  • Opts in to usage data: the WordPress user’s name and email, site URL and title, WordPress,
    PHP and plugin versions, site language, and whether the plugin is active or uninstalled.
    The list of plugins and themes is sent only if that permission is left on.
  • Opens the Upgrade (pricing) page, starts a trial, buys a plan or activates a license. With
    an active license, the paid version then checks Freemius for updates and license status.
  • Opens the Affiliation page in the plugin menu: the affiliate program terms are loaded from
    Freemius.
  • Submits the affiliate application form: the name, email, PayPal email, website domains and
    promotion details entered in the form are sent to Freemius. If the site is not connected
    to Freemius yet, it is connected with the email entered, with usage tracking off.
  • Clicks “Contact Us”: the Freemius contact form opens in a new browser tab.

Freemius terms: https://freemius.com/terms/ — privacy policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/ —
affiliate program terms: https://freemius.com/plugin/39395/ninhle-ai-sales-assistant/legal/affiliate-program/

Security

API keys are stored server-side and never sent to the browser; the settings screen
shows only a masked value. Every provider call is made from your server through the
WordPress REST API.

Database queries use $wpdb->prepare(). Every REST route declares a real
permission_callback, and the endpoints the AI uses as tools are internal-only –
they cannot be reached from outside the site. Visitor sessions use hashed tokens
and chat messages are rate limited per session.

Chat messages are rendered as DOM elements rather than injected HTML, and only
http and https links are ever made clickable, so content returned by the AI cannot
inject markup.

Please report security issues privately to the author rather than in a public forum.

Privacy

Conversations, contacts and leads are stored in your own WordPress database. The
plugin registers with Tools > Export Personal Data and Tools > Erase Personal Data,
so you can answer data-subject requests from WordPress itself. Message attachments
are purged on a configurable retention schedule. No data is sent anywhere except the
services listed under External services.

To count orders that followed a chat, the conversation number is saved in the
visitor’s WooCommerce shopping session when the assistant shows products or the
visitor clicks a product or cart link in the chat. An order placed within the
attribution window you choose (24 hours by default) is linked to that conversation.
The link, and the visitor’s answer to “Did this answer your question?”, are included
in the personal-data export and removed by the eraser. The plugin adds a suggested
paragraph about this to Settings > Privacy.
sections.installation:
1. Install from Plugins > Add New, or upload the plugin ZIP, then activate.
  2. Go to Ninhle AI Sales > Settings and enter an API key for your chosen AI provider (or choose local-only mode).
  3. Fill in the Business information and review the Sales playbook.
  4. Click “Sync products now” (or run wp ninhle-ai-sales-assistant sync-products) so the bot knows your catalog.
sections.faq:
Is this a free AI chatbot for WooCommerce?

Yes. The free version is complete and has no time limit or message cap from us. You pay only your
AI provider for your own API key, or use local-only mode with no key at all.

Can customers track their orders in the chat?

Yes. When a customer gives the order number together with the email address or phone number used
for the order, the assistant shows the order status in the chat. Without that proof it reveals
nothing about the order.

Which AI models does the chatbot work with?

Anthropic Claude, OpenAI and Google Gemini, with your own API key for each. You choose the
provider and can switch at any time.

Does the shopping assistant recommend products?

Yes. It searches your synced WooCommerce catalog, recommends products that match what the shopper
asked for and links to them. It only recommends products that exist in your store.

Do I need a paid AI subscription?

To use an AI provider, yes: you supply your own API key from Anthropic, OpenAI or Google
and are billed directly by that provider. Local-only mode needs no key.

How much does the AI cost to run?

It depends on the provider and model you choose, and you pay the provider directly. In our
internal test of 60 conversations with GPT-4o mini, the AI cost about US$0.0006 per conversation;
larger models cost more. The AI Value & Performance tab shows what your own store actually spent.

Can I try it without an API key?

Yes. Local-only mode answers product, cart and order questions from your store data without
calling any AI provider. Add a key later when you want full conversations.

Will it slow down my store?

The chat button is small, and the chat window and voice input load only when a visitor opens
the chat. Nothing is loaded from third-party servers unless you pick a Google font.

Is my store data sent to you?

No. Conversations, contacts and leads stay in your own WordPress database. Messages go only to
the AI provider you configure, and the other services listed under External services are used
only when you turn them on.

Does it work without WooCommerce?

The chat and lead capture work on any WordPress site. Product search, catalog grounding and
order lookup require WooCommerce.

Will it invent prices or stock?

No. The playbook forbids it and product facts come from lookups against your store. If the
catalog has not been synced, the bot is told to say so and offer a handoff instead of guessing.

What counts as an “AI-assisted order”?

An order placed within your attribution window (24 hours, 72 hours or 7 days) after the
customer received an answer with products from your store, or clicked a product or cart link
in the chat. Each order is counted once. Cancelled, failed and fully refunded orders are left
out, and partial refunds are deducted. AI-assisted does not mean the AI was the only reason
for the order.

Is anything in the free version locked?

No. Paid plans add separate code; the free version contains no locked or trial-limited features.

Where is the source code of the JavaScript files?

The files in assets/dist are built with Vite from the human-readable source shipped in the
plugin under src/JS (admin screens and chat widget). To rebuild them, run npm ci and then
npm run build in the plugin folder; the build configuration is in vite.config.ts and
package.json.
sections.changelog:
2.5.0

  • Added: optional voice input, off by default (“Let visitors speak their message” in Settings). Visitors tap the microphone and the browser turns their speech into text in the message box; they check it and send it themselves. The plugin never receives or stores audio. Shown only on HTTPS pages in browsers with speech recognition (not Firefox). Clear messages if the microphone is blocked, missing or not understood; typing always works.
  • Fixed: assistant replies no longer show raw formatting characters such as ** or -. Bold text, lists, tables, links and product images now display properly in the chat.
  • Fixed: product images could show as broken when the original file had been deleted from the server. The plugin now uses a resized copy that still exists, hides any image that cannot load, and loads same-site images over https on https pages.
  • Fixed: clicks on site-relative links in the chat are now counted for AI-assisted orders.
  • Changed: the chat window loads only when a visitor is about to open it, so pages load less JavaScript up front.
  • Changed: the Inbox shows readable statuses and senders, and the Rules Engine describes each rule in plain words instead of JSON.

2.4.1

  • Added: an Affiliation page in the plugin menu, for administrators, to apply for the Ninhle AI affiliate program: 30% commission on new sales and renewals, with a 45-day cookie. The program terms are loaded from Freemius when you open the page.
  • Added: an “Earn 30% commission” link on the Settings page, shown only to administrators. The automatic affiliate notice of the Freemius SDK is turned off.
  • Changed: the External services section of this readme lists every case in which the plugin contacts Freemius.

2.4.0

  • Added: AI Value & Performance tab – AI cost recorded per request with the provider’s usage and a dated price table, AI-assisted orders, and conversation outcomes (confirmed resolved, probably resolved, handed off, unresolved or unknown) with sample sizes. Figures start on the day you upgrade; older data is not backfilled.
  • Added: “Talk to a person” button in the chat widget. It hands the conversation to your team without calling the AI, and pressing it again does not create a second handoff.
  • Added: the widget shows a real status (AI assistant, waiting for a team member, a team member is helping you) and a short progress line while the assistant looks up products or orders.
  • Added: a “Did this answer your question?” prompt inside the chat, at most once per conversation, which visitors can skip.
  • Added: a line telling visitors they are chatting with an AI assistant, on by default and editable.
  • Added: WhatsApp and Telegram links next to Messenger, Zalo and phone; an option to hide the chat on the checkout page.
  • Changed: redesigned chat widget – simpler header, secondary actions in a “…” menu, no borders, text colour chosen for contrast on your brand colour, full screen on phones, keyboard support (Escape closes and returns focus).
  • Changed: on cart and checkout pages the chat button moves out of the way of the place-order button on phones.
  • Changed: revenue of AI-assisted orders is now part of the Starter plan.
  • Changed: the settings screen shows the model each provider actually uses and an estimated cost per conversation, and warns when a saved model has been retired.
  • Changed: Gemini replies count the model’s thinking tokens in the recorded cost, as Google bills them.
  • Changed: browser pop-ups (alert and confirm) in the admin screens and the widget are replaced by in-page messages.
  • Removed: Thinking mode and the prompt generator (“create prompt”) in the chat widget. Their settings are kept but no longer used.
  • Fixed: the assistant’s internal reasoning could appear in replies, the inbox and data exports; it is now removed before anything is saved, and older messages are cleaned when they are read.
  • Fixed: handoffs were counted only while a conversation was waiting for staff, so taking over or handing back made them disappear from the statistics.
  • Fixed: automation rules created in the Rules screen never ran.
  • Fixed: OpenAI errors (wrong or expired key, used-up quota, server errors) were treated as an empty answer, so the backup provider was never tried and nothing was logged. They are now reported as errors and the next provider in the chain answers.
  • Fixed: when the AI provider returned an empty answer, the visitor received no reply at all; they now get a short message asking them to rephrase.
  • Fixed: when every AI provider failed, the reply said the visitor had been passed to a colleague without doing so; it now says the assistant is briefly unavailable and points to “Talk to a person”.
  • Fixed: migration steps from earlier versions could not be recorded because their names were too long.
  • Fixed: the sample business details added at install (opening hours, cash on delivery, delivery times, 7-day returns) were given to shoppers as if they were the store’s own terms, even after the field was cleared. New installs start with this field empty, unchanged sample text is no longer used, and Settings asks you to enter your real details. Until then the assistant offers to check with your team instead of stating terms.
  • Fixed: “Restore default playbook” also replaced your business information with the sample text.
  • Fixed: product search results given to the assistant now state your store currency, so it no longer guesses one (for example “$” in a VND store), and product summaries use your currency format instead of always “đ”.
  • Fixed: products with variations (size, colour) had no price in the assistant’s product list, so it could not quote a price and price searches skipped them. The assistant now sees the price range and quotes a “from” price unless it has checked the chosen option.
  • Fixed: with “Delete data on uninstall” turned on, two plugin options were left in the database.
  • Fixed: on sites with WooCommerce, scheduling the plugin’s background tasks could log a “translation loading triggered too early” notice.

2.3.0

  • Added: WordPress personal-data export and erasure cover every table the plugin creates.
  • Added: declared compatibility with WooCommerce HPOS and the Cart/Checkout blocks.
  • Changed: the chat widget is one continuous white card (header, messages and composer) and fits narrow phone screens.
  • Changed: the widget uses the system font by default and loads Google Fonts only if you pick a Google font in the settings.
  • Changed: a chat session is created only when a visitor opens the chat, not on every page view. Returning visitors are no longer rate-limited, so visitors on shared mobile or office networks keep the chat button.
  • Fixed: on phones, the chat button could sit off-screen when the theme has content wider than the screen (for example a news ticker).
  • Fixed: automation rules could not be saved because the rules table was missing two columns; existing sites are repaired automatically.
  • Fixed: deleting an automation rule reported an error even though the rule was deleted.
  • Changed: the plugin is now named Ninhle AI Sales Assistant for WooCommerce.
  • Fixed: inline scripts attached to the admin and widget bundles were dropped when the bundles were loaded as ES modules.
  • Changed: Telegram notifications, product variations, coupon validation, provider failover, budget caps and the sales dashboard now ship only in the paid plans, as separate code.
  • Changed: translations come from translate.wordpress.org; the plugin no longer bundles its own translation files.
  • Fixed: handoff replies are now translatable instead of always Vietnamese.
  • Fixed: on/off settings saved as “on” were read back as “off”, so link reading, the prompt creator and the adaptive playbook never ran when enabled.
  • Fixed: the assistant could stop replying after looking up products or other tools.
  • Fixed: the assistant now reads PDF files customers attach, and reliably looks at attached images when using OpenAI.
  • Fixed: when link reading is on, files a customer uploads are no longer sent to the link-reading service.
  • Fixed: AI cost was recorded as zero when no model was chosen in the settings; the default model is now used for cost estimates.
  • Fixed: Gemini failed when the model field was left empty.
  • Fixed: attached files were never removed from conversations that were not closed, and deleting or clearing a conversation left its files on the server. Files sent in the chat are now deleted after the retention period, and immediately when their conversation is deleted or cleared.
  • Fixed: file uploads no longer require the PHP fileinfo extension.
  • Security: attachment paths are validated before files are read for the AI provider.
  • Changed: if processing a message fails unexpectedly, the visitor gets an apology instead of no reply.
  • Added: customers can paste an image (for example a screenshot) straight into the chat box.
  • Fixed: suggested follow-up questions sometimes appeared as raw “[SUGGESTIONS]” text instead of buttons.
  • Fixed: the response cache no longer stores answers that contain prices or stock status.
  • Security: YouTube caption downloads only go to youtube.com over HTTPS.
  • Changed: the free version no longer shows settings for features that exist only in the paid plans.
  • Fixed: the leads CSV export downloaded as escaped text instead of a spreadsheet; it now opens correctly in Excel, including accented names.
  • Changed: licensing and upgrade notices appear only on the plugin’s own admin pages.
  • Fixed: when coupon checking is not available, the assistant no longer tells customers a code is invalid; it asks them to enter it at checkout.
  • Security: chat responses are never stored by page caches (for example LiteSpeed Cache or a host CDN). A cached response could be served without a valid chat session, and visitors could miss the assistant’s reply.
  • Fixed: with Google Gemini or Anthropic Claude, product and order lookups could fail and the internal lookup command could appear in the chat.
  • Fixed: the default Gemini and Claude models had been retired by Google and Anthropic. The plugin now defaults to current models and ignores retired model names saved by earlier versions.
  • Changed: the default chat widget name is “Shop Assistant”; set your own name in the settings.
  • Added: the assistant knows the current date and time in your store’s timezone (Settings > General), so it can tell customers the date and take it into account for opening hours, delivery times and promotion end dates.

2.2.0

  • Added: three-tier licensing – Free, Starter and Pro – with Pro inheriting all Starter features.
  • Added: premium code moved to a separate directory so the Free build genuinely excludes it rather than hiding it.
  • Added: safe fallbacks so the Free build runs with no paid code present at all.
  • Changed: minimum WordPress raised to 6.3.

2.1.0

  • Changed: the admin interface is now English throughout; Vietnamese ships as a translation.
  • Changed: default widget tagline and policy fallbacks are English and brand-neutral.
  • Fixed: the Rules screen was calling REST helpers that did not exist, so every action on that tab failed.

2.0.0

  • Added: Freemius SDK for optional paid plans, supporting annual subscriptions and lifetime licenses.

text (https://jina.ai/legal/). YouTube links are read from youtube.com instead, to get the
video title and public transcript (https://policies.google.com/privacy,
https://www.youtube.com/t/terms). Leave this off if visitors might paste private links.

Google Fonts (optional) — only if you pick a Google font for the widget in the
settings. Visitors’ browsers then load that font from fonts.googleapis.com
(https://policies.google.com/privacy). The default font loads nothing from Google.

Voice input (optional, off by default) — only if you turn on “Let visitors speak their
message”. The microphone button uses the speech recognition built into the visitor’s own browser
(Web Speech API). Depending on the browser, the audio may be sent to the browser maker’s speech
recognition service, for example Google for Chrome (https://policies.google.com/privacy), Apple
for Safari (https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/) or Microsoft for Edge
(https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement). The plugin never receives, records or stores
audio; it only receives the text the visitor chooses to send.

Handoff webhook (optional) — only if you enter a webhook URL. On a handoff the plugin
sends the conversation ID, contact ID and handoff level to that URL, which you control.

Telegram (paid plans only, optional) — the free version contains no Telegram code. In
the Starter and Pro plans, if you enter a Telegram bot token and chat ID, new leads (name,
email, phone) and handoff requests (priority, issue, summary, conversation number) are sent
to api.telegram.org (https://telegram.org/privacy, https://telegram.org/tos).

Automation webhooks (Pro plan only, optional) — the free version contains no code for
this. In Pro, if you enter a webhook URL, lead and handoff events are posted to that URL,
which you control, signed with your secret.

Freemius (licensing, upgrades and affiliate program) — the plugin bundles the Freemius
SDK. Nothing is sent to Freemius from your storefront. The plugin contacts Freemius only
when an administrator does one of the following:

  • Opts in to usage data: the WordPress user’s name and email, site URL and title, WordPress,
    PHP and plugin versions, site language, and whether the plugin is active or uninstalled.
    The list of plugins and themes is sent only if that permission is left on.
  • Opens the Upgrade (pricing) page, starts a trial, buys a plan or activates a license. With
    an active license, the paid version then checks Freemius for updates and license status.
  • Opens the Affiliation page in the plugin menu: the affiliate program terms are loaded from
    Freemius.
  • Submits the affiliate application form: the name, email, PayPal email, website domains and
    promotion details entered in the form are sent to Freemius. If the site is not connected
    to Freemius yet, it is connected with the email entered, with usage tracking off.
  • Clicks “Contact Us”: the Freemius contact form opens in a new browser tab.

Freemius terms: https://freemius.com/terms/ — privacy policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/ —
affiliate program terms: https://freemius.com/plugin/39395/ninhle-ai-sales-assistant/legal/affiliate-program/

Security

API keys are stored server-side and never sent to the browser; the settings screen
shows only a masked value. Every provider call is made from your server through the
WordPress REST API.

Database queries use $wpdb->prepare(). Every REST route declares a real
permission_callback, and the endpoints the AI uses as tools are internal-only –
they cannot be reached from outside the site. Visitor sessions use hashed tokens
and chat messages are rate limited per session.

Chat messages are rendered as DOM elements rather than injected HTML, and only
http and https links are ever made clickable, so content returned by the AI cannot
inject markup.

Please report security issues privately to the author rather than in a public forum.

Privacy

Conversations, contacts and leads are stored in your own WordPress database. The
plugin registers with Tools > Export Personal Data and Tools > Erase Personal Data,
so you can answer data-subject requests from WordPress itself. Message attachments
are purged on a configurable retention schedule. No data is sent anywhere except the
services listed under External services.

To count orders that followed a chat, the conversation number is saved in the
visitor’s WooCommerce shopping session when the assistant shows products or the
visitor clicks a product or cart link in the chat. An order placed within the
attribution window you choose (24 hours by default) is linked to that conversation.
The link, and the visitor’s answer to “Did this answer your question?”, are included
in the personal-data export and removed by the eraser. The plugin adds a suggested
paragraph about this to Settings > Privacy.
